MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL
  HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING

    Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana
   (PMMSY)

        Approval and Duration: Approved by Union Cabinet on 20 May 2020. Implemented during
       2020-21 to 2024-25 and later extended to 2025-26.

         Total Outlay: Rs. 20,050 crore (Central share Rs. 9,407 crore, State share Rs. 4,880 crore,
         Beneficiary contribution Rs. 5,763 crore).

        Objectives:

          1. Bridge critical gaps across the fisheries value chain.

          2. Enhance fish production and productivity.

          3. Modernize post-harvest management, quality, safety and traceability.

          4. Welfare of fishers, fish farmers and workers.

          5. Generate employment in fisheries and aquaculture.

       Funding Pattern:

         Centrally Sponsored Scheme components follow 60:40 Centre State ratio for general
         States, 90:10 for North Eastern and Himalayan States, and 100% Central funding for Union
          Territories.

       Components:

          1. Fisheries clusters and hubs.

          2. Fishing harbours and landing centres.

          3. Cold chain infrastructure such as ice plants, cold storages, reefers.

          4. Processing and value addition units.

          5. Fish markets and transport facilities.

          6. Brood banks, hatcheries and seed infrastructure.





MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING                                                                                                            1

7. Insurance and welfare measures for fishers.

          8. Safety and quality systems.

          9. National Fisheries Digital Platform for registration and benefit delivery.

       Sub-Scheme:

       Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah Yojana introduced in 2023-24 for
        implementation up to 2026-27 with an outlay of Rs. 6,000 crore.

    Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah
    Yojana (PM-MKSSY)

        Type: Central Sector sub-scheme under PMMSY.

        Period and Outlay: 2023-24 to 2026-27 with an outlay of Rs. 6,000 crore.

        Objectives and Components:

          1. Formalization of fisheries sector and access to working capital finance through National
             Fisheries Digital Platform.

          2. One-time incentive for aquaculture insurance with both basic and enhanced covers.

          3. Performance grants for fisheries and aquaculture micro-enterprises to improve
             efficiency of value chain.

          4. Support for food safety and quality systems including traceability and standards.

          5. Project management, monitoring and evaluation.


    Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure
    Development Fund (FIDF)

       Launch: 2018-19.

         Total Corpus: Rs. 7,522.48 crore.

        Purpose: Development of fisheries infrastructure and concessional finance for eligible
         projects.

         Eligible Infrastructure: Fishing harbours, landing centres, brood banks, hatcheries, fish
       seed farms, cold storages, ice plants, reefer transport, processing units, fish markets,
         training centres.





MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING                                                                        2

Eligible Entities: States and Union Territories, State entities, cooperatives, self-help groups,
        farmer producer organisations, panchayati raj institutions, private entrepreneurs.

         Financial Terms:

          1. Interest subvention up to 3% per annum.

          2. Lending rate of Nodal Loaning Entities not lower than 5% per annum.

          3. Loan up to 80% of project cost.

          4. Beneficiary margin of 20%.

          5. Repayment period of up to 12 years including 2 years moratorium.


    Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM)

       Launch: December 2014, continued under Development Programmes 2021-22 to 2025-26.

        Outlay: Rs. 2,400 crore.

        Objectives:

          1. Conservation and genetic improvement of indigenous bovine breeds.

          2. Enhance milk productivity and yield.

          3. Strengthen artificial insemination and semen stations.

          4. Support rural poor through dairy development.

       Components:

          1. Breed improvement using artificial insemination and in-vitro fertilisation.

          2. Support for semen stations and breed multiplication farms.

          3. Subsidy of Rs. 5,000 per assured pregnancy under IVF.

          4. Subsidy of Rs. 750 or 50 percent of cost per assured pregnancy using sex-sorted
          semen.

          5. Conservation of indigenous breeds.

          6. Capacity building and farmer awareness.

       Funding Pattern: 60:40 for general States, 90:10 for North Eastern and Himalayan States,
       100 percent Central for Union Territories.

    National Livestock Mission (NLM)




MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING                                                                       3

Launch: Introduced in 2014-15, restructured for 2021-22 to 2025-26.

        Outlay: Approximately Rs. 2,300 crore.

        Objectives:

          1. Promote sustainable livestock development including sheep, goat, pig and poultry.

          2. Improve feed and fodder availability.

          3. Support entrepreneurship and employment generation.

          4. Improve productivity and risk management.

        Sub-Missions:

          1. Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry.

          2. Feed and Fodder Development.

          3. Extension and Innovation including livestock insurance.

        Entrepreneurship Support:

       50 percent subsidy for individuals, self-help groups, joint liability groups, farmer producer
         organisations and Section 8 companies for setting up poultry hatcheries, brooder units,
       sheep and goat multiplication farms, piggery farms and feed or fodder units.

       Funding Pattern: 60:40 Centre State for general States, 90:10 for North Eastern and
        Himalayan States, 100 percent for Union Territories.

    National Programme for Dairy Development
    (NPDD)

        Period: 2021-22 to 2025-26.

        Structure: Two components.

       Component A:

          1. Infrastructure for quality milk testing.

          2. Bulk milk coolers and chilling facilities.

          3. Processing facilities, ICT, traceability, clean milk production, training and awareness.

          4. Research and development.

       Funding Pattern for Component A: 60:40 Centre State, 90:10 for North Eastern and
        Himalayan States, 100 percent for Union Territories, and 100 percent Central for R and D,
        ICT and training.





MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING                                                                    4

Component B – Dairying through Cooperatives: Supported with external assistance from
       Japan International Cooperation Agency, focused on nine States including Andhra Pradesh,
         Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and
       West Bengal.

    Supporting Dairy Cooperatives and Farmer
    Producer Organisations (SDCFPO)

        Type: Central Sector component under Infrastructure Development Fund.

        Outlay: Rs. 500 crore during 2021-22 to 2025-26.

        Objectives:

          1. Provide soft loans to dairy cooperatives and farmer producer organisations for working
              capital.

          2. Maintain procurement and timely payments to dairy farmers during crises.

       Key Features:

          1. Interest subvention of 2 percent per annum with additional 2 percent for prompt
           repayment.

          2. Eligible products include Skimmed Milk Powder, Whole Milk Powder, White Butter and
           Ghee.


    Dairy Processing and Infrastructure
    Development Fund (DIDF)

       Launch: 2017.

        Objective: Modernisation and creation of dairy processing and chilling infrastructure.

        Status: Subsumed into Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund in 2024.

        9) Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)

       Launch: June 2020 under Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan.

        Outlay: Rs. 29,610.25 crore.

        Objectives:

          1. Encourage investment by entrepreneurs, MSMEs, FPOs, Section 8 companies and
            cooperatives.





MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING                                                                        5

2. Develop dairy and meat processing infrastructure.

          3. Establish animal feed plants.

          4. Promote breed multiplication farms.

          5. Support veterinary vaccine and drug production.

          6. Develop waste to wealth facilities such as biogas plants.

          7. Primary wool processing units.

         Financial Features:

          1. Interest subvention of 3%.

          2. Repayment period up to 10 years including moratorium.

          3. Loan up to 90% of project cost.

          4. Credit guarantee up to 25% for MSMEs and cooperatives.


    Livestock Health and Disease Control
   Programme (LHDCP)

        Period: 2021-22 to 2025-26.

        Objectives:

          1. Control and eradicate major livestock diseases including Foot and Mouth Disease,
             Brucellosis, Peste des Petits Ruminants and Classical Swine Fever.

          2. Strengthen veterinary infrastructure, disease surveillance and vaccination.

          3. Provide mobile veterinary units.

       Sub-Programmes:

          1. Critical Animal Disease Control Programme for eradication of PPR and CSF.

          2. Establishment and Strengthening of Veterinary Hospitals and Dispensaries including
           Mobile Veterinary Units.

          3. Assistance to States for Control of Animal Diseases for state prioritised diseases.

       Funding Pattern:

       100 percent Central for Critical Animal Disease Control Programme and non-recurring
        expenditure under Establishment and Strengthening of Veterinary Hospitals.





MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING                                                                      6

60:40 Centre State for other components.

        90:10 for North Eastern and Himalayan States.

       100 percent Central for Union Territories.

        National Animal Disease Control Programme (within LHDCP): 100 percent Centrally
        funded, outlay of Rs. 13,343 crore for five years from 2019-20 to 2023-24, targeting
         eradication of Foot and Mouth Disease and Brucellosis by 2030.

MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS

    Post Matric Scholarship Scheme For The
    Students Belonging To Scheduled Tribe For
    Studies In India

       Overview & Purpose:

            This is a centrally sponsored scholarship administered by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
           (MoTA) and implemented through respective State/UT governments via portals like the
            National Scholarship Portal (NSP).

                    It covers education from Class X (post-matric) up to postgraduate level, including
             technical and professional courses.

                Its key objective is to ensure that eligible ST students receive timely financial support to
           pursue higher education.

          Eligibility Criteria:

            Domicile: Student must belong to an ST category and reside in the state/UT they apply
            from.

           Education Level: Applicable to students pursuing any post‑matriculation course—
             Class XI onwards, including diplomas, graduate, postgraduate, and research degrees.

          Annual Family Income Cap: ₹2.50 lakh from all sources.

          One-Time Registration (OTR) on NSP is mandatory.

           Students already receiving a scholarship under MoTA’s Top Class or National Fellowship
          schemes are not eligible to avail this scholarship simultaneously.

      Scheme Components & Benefits:

       Component 1: Fee Reimbursement

           Covers compulsory fees (tuition, etc.) charged by institutions, subject to state-defined
               limits.

       Component 2: Maintenance Allowance

    National Overseas Scholarship For Scheduled
    Tribes (ST) Students

           1. Scheme Overview:

         A Central Sector Scheme by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, implemented through Indian
           Embassies/Missions under the Ministry of External Affairs, aimed at supporting regular,
              full-time ST students for Master’s, Ph.D., and Post-Doctoral research programs abroad.

            Bachelor-level studies are not covered.

          20 awards are granted annually:

          1. 17 for general ST candidates

          2. 3 for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG)

        30% of awards reserved for female candidates, with unused slots transferable to male
           candidates if necessary.

         2. Eligibility Criteria:

            Domicile: Must be from the Scheduled Tribes.

           Course Level: Only PG, Ph.D., or Post-Doctoral programs abroad.

          Academic Minimum: At least 55% marks or equivalent in the relevant qualifying exam.

               For Master’s: required marks in Bachelor’s degree.

               For Ph.D.: required marks in Master’s degree.





MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                3

For Post-Doctoral: Master’s with Ph.D

       Age Limits (as on July 1 of selection year):

             Master’s: ≤ 32 years

             Ph.D.: ≤ 35 years

            Post-Doctoral: ≤ 38 years

        Family Income: Must not exceed ₹6,00,000 per annum.

           Only parental income is counted; earnings of siblings or others are excluded.

          Orphans under guardianship are exempt from income criteria.

        Family Restriction: Only one child per family may avail—one-time scholarship per individual.

         3. Fields of Study & Annual Slots:

          FIELD OF STUFY              SLOTS PER YEAR

        STEM (Science, Engineering,
                                           10
          Technology, Mathematics)

         Management, Economics,
                                  4
           Finance, Law

           Agriculture / Medicine          4

          Humanities / Social Sciences /
                                    2
           Fine Arts

         4. Duration of Assistance:

         Financial support continues until course completion or prescribed maximum duration,
        whichever is earlier:

             Master’s: 1 or 2 years

             Ph.D.: Up to 4 years

            Post-Doctoral: Up to 2 years

         5. Scholarship Components & Benefits:

           Annual Maintenance Allowance:

           USD 15,400 (or equivalent)

           GBP 9,900 for the UK

           Annual Contingency & Equipment Allowance:

      USD 1,532 (US)





MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                            4

GBP 1,116 (UK)

         Tuition & Non-Refundable Fees: Covered as per actuals

        Visa Fees: Actual charges reimbursed in INR.

        Medical Insurance: Actual premium, subject to embassy discretion.

          Air Passage: Economy-class round-trip airfare from India to institution and back.

        Local Travel: Second-class rail fare from arrival to institution; permissible alternate travel
       modes where applicable.

          Poll Tax & Incidental Journey Expenses: Actual poll tax reimbursed; incidental expenses up
         to USD 20 or equivalent.

         6. Selection Process:

            Applications are via the National Overseas Scholarship Portal (NOSP):
             overseas.tribal.gov.in.

            Multi-stage merit evaluation:

          1. Priority to applicants already admitted and enrolled in QS top-1,000 universities, ranked
          by institution.

          2. Then, applicants with admission offers (not yet joined) from QS top-1,000.

          3. Remaining slots via expert committee interviews—preference for GRE/GMAT/TOEFL-
             qualified candidates.

           7. Other Conditions & Obligations:

          Bound by agreements with the Government of India and Indian Mission; no change of
              institute or course permitted post-selection.

          Overpayments must be refunded.

         Upon course completion, awardees must upload completion details and a study brief in
            the NOS portal's Alumni Module before return travel is booked.

          Awards may be cancelled and funds recovered if:

               Misrepresentation or document falsification occurs.

               Candidate fails to complete the course (unless due to certified ill-health).

               Involvement in illegal/narcotic/antinational activities.

    National Fellowship & Scholarship For Higher
    Education Of Scheduled Tribe (ST) Students




MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                  5

Scheme architecture:

           Type: Central Sector Scheme with two distinct parts administered by the Ministry of
              Tribal Affairs (MoTA).

             Part-A: Fellowship (NFST) — for M.Phil/Ph.D (including integrated M.Phil+Ph.D).

             Part-B: Scholarship (“Top Class”) — for Graduate & Post-Graduate programs in notified
           premier institutes in professional & other fields.

      Part A – National Fellowship (NFST)

        Objective:

          To provide financial assistance to Scheduled Tribe students who have completed a
           postgraduate degree and want to pursue M.Phil/Ph.D on a full-time basis in recognized
            Indian universities/institutes.

       Coverage:

          750 fresh fellowships are awarded every year.

           Vacant slots are carried forward to the next academic year.

           There is no state-wise or university-wise cap on slots.

          Eligibility:

          Must belong to Scheduled Tribe (ST).

          Minimum 55% marks in post-graduation.

         Age limit: 36 years (as on 1 July of the selection year).

         No family income criteria.

           Admission should be in universities/institutes recognized under UGC Act, Central/State
           funded institutions, or Institutes of National Importance.

        Duration:

            M.Phil – 2 years.

           Ph.D – 5 years.

            Integrated M.Phil + Ph.D – 5 years.

        Fellowship Amount (UGC equivalent rates – effective Jan 2023)

            M.Phil/Ph.D (first 2 years): ₹37,000 per month.

           Ph.D (remaining 3 years): ₹42,000 per month.

           Contingency Grant:




MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                6

Humanities/Social Sciences – ₹10,000 per year (initial 2 years), ₹20,500 per year
                (next 3 years).

               Sciences/Engineering/Technology – ₹12,000 per year (initial 2 years), ₹25,000 per
               year (next 3 years).

          HRA: As per Government/UGC rates (30% / 20% / 10% of basic depending on city
            category).

           Divyangjan Allowance: ₹2,000 per month.

       Key Conditions:

         No other government fellowship can be availed for the same study.

                   If hostel accommodation is provided, HRA is not payable (only hostel fee can be
            reimbursed).

      Part B – Top Class Scholarship (for Higher Education in Notified
       Institutes)

        Objective:

       To encourage meritorious ST students to pursue graduate and postgraduate professional
       courses in premier institutions identified by the Ministry.

       Coverage:

            Applicable to notified premier institutes.

         Number of notified institutes has been expanded to 265 (2025 update).

            Scholarship continues till the completion of the course, subject to satisfactory
           performance.

          Eligibility:

          Must belong to Scheduled Tribe (ST).

           Admitted on merit into a course in a notified institute.

           Annual family income ≤ ₹6,00,000.

           Not eligible if admitted under management quota.

           Students already availing Post Matric Scholarship or other MoTA schemes cannot apply
              (to avoid duplication).

         Benefits:

          1. Fee Coverage:

                   Full admission and tuition fees in government institutions.




MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                         7

In private institutions, fee ceiling of ₹2.5 lakh per annum per student.

          2. Books & Stationery: ₹5,000 per year.

          3. Living Expenses: ₹3,000 per month.

          4. Computer/Accessories: ₹45,000 one-time during the course (no voucher needed).

        Administration:

            Applications are invited through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP).

          One-Time Registration (OTR) is mandatory.

            Scholarships are disbursed directly into student bank accounts through DBT.

    Pre- Matric Scholarship For Scheduled Tribe
    Students

           1. Purpose:

         A Centrally Sponsored Scheme, implemented through State/UT governments via the
            National Scholarship Portal (NSP) or respective state portals.

          Aims to support ST students in Classes 9 and 10 to reduce dropout rates during the
              transition from elementary to secondary education.

           Covers only one academic year per class; the scholarship is not provided again if the
            student repeats the class.

         2. Eligibility Criteria:

          Must belong to a Scheduled Tribe (ST), and be domiciled in the state/UT to which the
             application is made.

          Must be studying in Class IX or X in a government school, or one recognized by the
           government or a State/Central Board of Secondary Education.

           Annual family income (from all sources) must not exceed ₹2.5 lakh.

           Not eligible if availing any other government scholarship.

         3. Benefits:

         a. Regular Scholarship (for 10 months per year)

          Day Scholars: ₹225 per month

             Hostellers: ₹525 per month

         b. Books & Ad hoc Grant (annual)





MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                8

Day Scholars: ₹750

             Hostellers: ₹1,000

         c. Additional Allowances (for students with disabilities in private unaided schools only)

           Reader Allowance (for blind students): ₹160 per month

            Transport Allowance (if the student does not stay in the school hostel): ₹160 per month

            Escort Allowance (for severely disabled students, ≥80% disability or low extremity
               disability): ₹160 per month

           Helper Allowance (for a helper assisting a severely orthopedically handicapped student
              in hostel): ₹160 per month

           Coaching Allowance (for mentally retarded or mentally ill students): ₹240 per month

    Vocational Training in Tribal Areas

           1. Purpose & Coverage:

          The scheme aims to enhance the socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribe (ST)
           youth—including Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)—by providing skill
           development in traditional and modern occupations tailored to regional educational
           backgrounds, market trends, and employment potential.

           While applicable nationwide, priority is accorded to remote tribal regions, territories
            inhabited by PVTGs, and areas affected by extremism.

         2. Scheme Components:

          Any public or qualified private institution—including State/UT governments, NGOs, and
            vocational training organizations—may establish vocational training centres (VTCs),
            regardless of participants’ domicile.

              Institutions must assess local employment needs considering participants’ educational
              qualifications, regional industries, and market demand prior to introducing trades.

             Training must be linked to recognized certification frameworks:

           MES (Modular Employable Skills) via Regional Directorate of Apprenticeship
                 Training,

           CTS (Craftsmen Training Scheme) under NCVT.

              Institutions should facilitate job placements and self-employment through partnerships
            with placement services, the NSTFDC, banks, and microfinance institutions. Priority is
            given to organizations that guarantee placement post-training.

            At least 33% of training seats must be reserved for tribal women.

          The scheme provides 100% grant-in-aid to qualified institutions. Disbursal to
           governments occurs in one instalment per year; NGOs and private institutions may
            receive funds in two instalments as per General Financial Rules.

         3. Benefits & Financial Norms:

        Recurring Costs (per trainee annually)

           ₹30,000 includes:

                Stipend: ₹700/month

               Tools/raw materials: ₹1,600





MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                                 10

Faculty/support remuneration

               Boarding, lodging, electricity, water, etc.

            Building rent/maintenance:

                        If rented: up to ₹10,000/month (with state PWD certification).

                        If owned: up to 10% of PWD-assessed rental value per annum.

       Non-Recurring Costs

           ₹2.40 lakh for setting up training across five trades (₹48,000 per trade), once every
              five years.

         4. Eligible Institutions:

       The following entities are eligible for scheme grants, subject to a minimum of three years of
         registration or operational experience:

            State Governments and UT Administrations

           Government-established autonomous bodies (under statute or Society Registration Act)

            Educational institutions, local bodies, cooperatives

            Public Trusts (registered over three years ago)

             Private recognized institutions (conducting vocational training for at least three years)

            Industry associations like ASSOCHAM, CII, FICCI (with plans for placements)

         NGOs/VOs registered for at least three years, with experience in ST welfare, community
             mobilization, and a sound reputation—especially in PTG or remote areas.

   Scheme of Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary
    Organisations Working for the Welfare of
    Scheduled Tribes

           1. Objective & Scope:

         A Central Sector Scheme aimed at extending government welfare efforts through
            voluntary organizations (VOs/NGOs) in underserved tribal areas.

          Seeks to bridge gaps in essential sectors such as education, health, drinking water,
             agro-horticulture, livelihood, social security, and other innovative community
           development efforts.





MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                                                                 11

Emphasis is placed on projects benefiting Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
           (PVTGs), Left-Wing Extremism (LWE)-affected districts, and remote or underserved
               tribal areas.

         2. Eligible Project Categories:

        Voluntary organizations can receive grants for projects in the following sectors:

           Education: Running and maintaining residential/non-residential schools, hostels;
           sponsoring tribal girls from Northeast and island regions (e.g. study in reputed
              institutions).

            Health: Running or maintaining hospitals/dispensaries (with ≥10 beds); mobile
           dispensary units.

            Livelihood: Supporting activities in agriculture, fishery, dairy, animal husbandry, water
            conservation, organic farming, etc.

          Emergency response: During disasters or pandemics, ministry may provide emergency
             aid (health services, food, water), in consultation with financial authorities.

         3. Eligibility Criteria for Organizations:

        Organizations applying for grants must:

          Be a registered VO/NGO engaged in ST welfare under the Societies Registration Act,
            Trust Act, or similar statutes, and registered with NGO-Darpan.

          Have a minimum of three years' operational experience in relevant welfare projects.

           Implement the project directly (no sub-granting).

           Sign an MoU with MoTA and comply with all scheme terms.

         Open an Aadhaar-linked joint account (President & Secretary) for fund disbursement.

           Hold PAN, TAN, filed ITRs for last three years, and be registered under Income Tax Act
            §12A.

           Not be blacklisted or under investigation; must have adequate financial
              capability/credibility.

            Maintain transparency via disclosures of trustees and financials.

           Serve at least 75 ST beneficiaries per project (smaller projects ≥25 beneficiaries may
          be approved for PTG areas with justification).

         4. Funding Pattern:

         100% grant-in-aid for projects in Scheduled Areas.





MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                                    12

90% central funding and 10% NGO share in other areas; exceptions possible at
             Ministry’s discretion.

          5. Application & Monitoring Process:

         NGOs must submit project proposals to the State Tribal Welfare Department, which in
             turn recommends shortlisted projects through the State Committee for Supporting
            Voluntary Efforts (SCSVE).

          The Ministry does not accept direct applications.

           Funding follows General Financial Rules (GFR)—including a 10% mandatory NGO
             contribution and execution of a surety bond on non-judicial stamp paper.

           Release of funds is made to designated accounts (state-level and project-level
            accounts), with facility for reallocation of unutilized funds mid-year.

         NGOs must submit bi-annual progress reports (April & October), and projects undergo
            monitoring and inspections by District Collectors and Ministry officials; 2% of the
           scheme’s budget is allocated to monitoring. Boards acknowledging MoTA’s support
          must be displayed onsite.

          6. Financial Norms & Project Types:

            Detailed financial norms are prescribed for each sector including residential schools,
             hostels, mobile libraries, training centers, health infrastructure, etc., under Appendix-I.

            Non-recurring costs (once in five years) and recurring costs (annual operations) are
            defined per project type.

            Beneficiary numbers have flexibility; projects should scale to ≥100 beneficiaries within a
            year where applicable.

   Scheme of Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary
    Organisations Working for the Welfare of
    Scheduled Tribes

           1. Introduction:

            This is a Central Sector Scheme launched by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA),
          Government of India.

          The scheme aims to extend the reach of welfare programmes and fill gaps in service-
             deficient tribal areas through voluntary organisations (VOs/NGOs).





MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                                   13

Focus areas include education, health, drinking water, livelihood, agro-horticulture,
             social security, and other innovative activities that directly improve the socio-economic
           development and livelihoods of Scheduled Tribes (STs).

         2. Objectives:

          To provide essential services in remote and underserved tribal areas.

          To promote socio-economic upliftment and overall development of ST communities.

          To support innovative and community-based projects in welfare and livelihood
            generation.

         3. Benefits & Project Categories:

       Broad categories of projects supported under the scheme:

        Education Sector

          1. Running and maintenance of non-residential/residential schools and hostels.

          2. Sponsoring tribal girls from North Eastern States (Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram,
            Manipur, Nagaland, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim) and Union Territories
          (Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep) for study in reputed institutions.

        Health Sector

         3. Running/maintenance of hospitals or dispensaries with at least 10 beds.

         4. Mobile dispensary units for tribal areas.

        Livelihood Sector

          5. Enhancement of livelihood and income generation opportunities through capacity
         building and infrastructure in agriculture, fishery, dairy, animal husbandry, water
        conservation, and organic/natural farming.

        Other provisions

           During natural calamities or pandemics, NGOs may provide emergency health services,
            food, and water, with MoTA’s approval.

              Priority is given to projects benefiting Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs),
           LWE-affected districts, and remote tribal areas.

           Grants are provided as per fixed financial norms for recurring and non-recurring costs.

         4. Eligibility for Organisations:

        Applicant organisations must meet the following criteria:

          Be a registered VO/NGO engaged in ST welfare.





MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                                14

Registration under Societies Registration Act, 1860, State Society Acts, Public Trusts, or
              similar laws.

           Mandatory registration on the NGO-Darpan portal (NITI Aayog).

            At least 3 years of experience in similar projects.

          The organisation must implement projects directly (no sub-granting).

          Must sign a MoU with MoTA before receiving grants.

          Must have an Aadhaar-linked joint bank account (President & Secretary/authorised
             signatories).

           Possession of PAN, TAN, and filing of ITRs for the past 3 years.

          Must be registered under Section 12A of the Income Tax Act.

           Should not be bankrupt or under investigation by CBI/ED/CBIC or any other agency.

          Must have the financial capacity to partially co-finance the project, since MoTA grants
            are restricted to core activities.

          Must submit details of trustees, promoters, and management committee with PAN and
           Aadhaar details.

           Should not be blacklisted by NITI Aayog or any government ministry.

         5. Beneficiary Requirement:

         A project must cover at least 75 ST beneficiaries.

             Exceptionally, with State Tribal Welfare Department’s justification and Minister’s
            approval, a project with minimum 25 ST students may be allowed for educational
             projects.

         6. Funding Pattern:

           Grants are released according to norms and ceilings for different projects.

           Covers recurring (operational) and non-recurring (capital) expenses as per Annexure
             guidelines.

          Funds are released in instalments in line with General Financial Rules (GFR).

     Institutional Support for Development and
    Marketing of Tribal Products/Produce

           1. Introduction:





MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                                    15

Launched in 2014–15 by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA).

          The scheme was formed by merging two earlier schemes:

              1. Market Development of Tribal Products/Produce

              2. Grant-in-Aid to State Tribal Development Cooperative Corporations for Minor Forest
              Produce Operation

             Objective: To provide comprehensive institutional support for the entire value chain of
               tribal products—from production, development, preservation of traditional heritage,
            marketing, to fair price realization.

         2. Scope of the Scheme:

           Supports both forest-based produce (like Minor Forest Produce) and agriculture-based
           produce of tribal communities.

            Assists institutions working in production, processing, marketing, design development,
          and infrastructure creation.

          Aims to ensure fair pricing, sustainable marketing, and livelihood enhancement for
               tribals.

           Encourages information sharing with Gram Panchayats/Gram Sabhas, skill
           development, and preservation of tribal heritage.

         3. Major Activities Supported:

         a) Market Intervention

             Fixation of equitable prices for tribal products (natural and handmade).

           Procurement by State agencies as a safety net, not monopoly.

           Support during harvest seasons when prices fall.

            Price information dissemination for better decision-making.

            Sale of tribal products in urban and external markets to boost demand.

              Activities include:

               Grading, standardization, source certification, and patenting.

               Branding and promotional campaigns.

         b) Training & Skill Upgradation

             Training in improved production, higher-grade and high-value products.

          Focus on quality enhancement and design improvement.





MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                                   16

Development of new utilitarian and export-oriented products.

            Collaboration with Agriculture, Horticulture, Handlooms, Handicrafts, Khadi and Village
             Industries for training and technology support.

         c) Research, Development & Intellectual Property (R&D/IPR)

        New product development and improved processes.

              Scientific harvesting practices.

           Documentation of traditional knowledge and crafts for IPR/royalty benefits and
            protection from piracy.

            Preservation of tangible and intangible heritage for tourism promotion.

         d) Supply Chain & Infrastructure Development

            Establishment of warehouses, godowns, cold storages, and processing industries for
            value addition.

            Product-specific warehousing facilities at institutional and village levels.

             Training on warehousing and supply chain management.

         e) Trade Information System

            Capturing and disseminating data on production, collection, sources, and market
             potential of tribal products.

          Web-enabled services, mobile/SMS-based information systems.

           f) Branding & Export Promotion

            Creating brands for tribal produce/products.

           Developing product designs for domestic and export markets.

           Support for exports through product-specific initiatives.

         4. Eligibility:

          Institutions eligible for support include:

          1. TRIFED (Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India Ltd.)

          2. State Tribal Development Cooperative Corporations (STDCCs)

          3. State Forest Development Corporations (SFDCs)

          4. Minor Forest Produce (Trading & Development) Federations (MFPTDFs)

          5. Other institutions involved in:

               Product design and development




MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS                                                                                                                         17

Export processing

                Training of tribal producers

                Patenting and trademarking

               Research, GI certification, and related activities

         5. Key Benefits for Tribal Communities:

           Assured fair prices through institutional procurement and market support.

          Enhanced skills, designs, and quality of tribal products.

           Development of brands and export potential.

            Preservation of traditional heritage and knowledge.

             Infrastructure support (storage, processing, marketing hubs).

           Improved livelihood opportunities and reduction of exploitation by middlemen.
